chunks: And by this chain, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Suleiman ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

None of you should recite the Iqamah for the Salat while he is walking, nor while riding, nor lying down, unless he is sick; and let him be stable/established in the Iqamah just as he is stable in the Salat, for indeed when he begins the Iqamah, he is in the Salat.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the posture of the person reciting the Iqamah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the Iqamah caller must stand firmly, mirroring the physical stability required during prayer, unless illness prevents it. This ruling underscores the theological view that the Iqamah is not merely a preparatory announcement but an integral extension of the Salat itself, as the caller enters the state of prayer upon beginning the call. This emphasis on bodily presence and stability reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking ritual precision with spiritual intent.

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Suleyman Bin Salih, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘None of you should recite an Iqamah for the Salāt while he is walking, nor while riding, nor lying down, unless he happens to be sick; and let him be able upon regarding the Iqamah just as he is able upon regarding the Salāt. So when he takes to the Iqamah, so he is in the Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 21. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith the following is narrated from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah from Sulayman ibn Salih who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

No one among you says ‘Iqamah for Salah (prayer) when walking, riding or resting unless one is ill. One remains well placed during ‘Iqamah like in Salah (prayer). In ‘Iqamah one is in Salah (prayer).’”
